A1.justification: Both readable 11-page PDFs describe the same work, with corresponding text, equations, figures and tables. Neither supplied PDF includes an appendix, although both mention supplementary materials.

before.justification: v1 reports original architecture and training ablations, benchmark evaluations, qualitative predictions and runtime measurements in Tables 2–7 and Figures 6–7.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experiments and measured outcomes in Tables 2–7 and Figures 6–7.

M1.justification: The backbone, serial 3D-then-2D aggregation, disparity estimation and three-stage training remain unchanged. Section 3.1 revises the aggregation rationale without changing the procedure or Equation 2.

E1.justification: The synthetic and real-world training datasets and evaluation coverage are unchanged, including KITTI, ETH3D, Middlebury and DrivingStereo weather. StereoCarla is newly cited but is not reported as used.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains identical in Tables 3–7 and Figure 7, including the efficient-model comparisons and the FoundationStereo teacher comparison.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1–4.3 and the table captions retain the same sample counts, resolutions, metrics, training budgets and evaluation procedures. No new experimental protocol is introduced.

E4.justification: The aggregation and training ablations in Table 2, weather evaluation in Table 4, transfer of the training strategy in Table 6 and qualitative analyses are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical entries and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, Table 3 retains final-model KITTI 2012/2015 D1 errors of 3.04/3.87, ETH3D Bad-1 of 3.53 and Middlebury Bad-2 of 7.51.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5 and their mathematical definitions remain unchanged. The revised aggregation explanation introduces no formal assumption, derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about efficient zero-shot stereo, hybrid aggregation, three-stage training and accuracy relative to computational cost.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 replaces the explanation that limited spatial receptive fields restrict generalization with a qualified explanation about missing explicit disparity continuity. It now describes 3D aggregation as joint spatial/disparity reasoning and 2D aggregation as spatial refinement. Section 4.5 limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation and access information remain unchanged, including the project link, 150K/50K/100K training steps, batch size 176, A100 hardware, learning rate, crop sizes and maximum disparity.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 adds StereoCarla as reference 21 in the cost-aggregation literature. Existing works are retained; the other bibliography changes update publication metadata and numbering without revising research positioning.

P1.justification: The opening cost-aggregation paragraph in Section 3.1 is rewritten and slightly expanded. Bibliographic metadata and the arXiv version/date header are updated; section organization and the remaining narrative are preserved.

P2.justification: The expanded paragraph slightly changes column flow and equation placement on page 4, while the bibliography reflows across pages 9–11. Figures 1–7 and Tables 1–7 retain their content and visual design.

improvement.justification: Section 3.1 provides a clearer, more appropriately qualified explanation of the unchanged architecture: it distinguishes explicit disparity structure from spatial refinement instead of attributing the limitation to spatial receptive fields. This improves technical clarity, while the method, empirical support and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
